title: Continuous Mirror supermask versus binary task masks
hypothesis: For a family of task subnetworks generated by low-dimensional functional views, a shared continuous mask basis plus compact task codes can preserve mask function quality while using fewer serialized bytes than independent packed binary masks; generic PCA may explain any gain.
physical_object: fixed 4096-coordinate backbone mask space shared by 64 task functions
mirror_coordinate: two continuous task coefficients over a shared score basis, thresholded to binary subnetwork
controls: independent packed binary task masks (SupSup/Piggyback storage control)
continuous Mirror basis plus fp16 task codes
generic rank-2 PCA of binary masks with mean
generic rank-2 logistic matrix factorization fitted to task masks

development.selection_metric: actual serialized payload bytes, mask bit agreement, function output NRMSE

paid_objects: Mirror score basis and task codes in fp16
PCA mean, basis and task codes in fp16

success_gate: Mirror query NRMSE <=0.05 with at least 30% fewer bytes than packed binary masks; Mirror-specific claim additionally beats generic PCA and fitted logistic factorization at comparable bytes.
failure_gate: Mirror fails quality gate or does not save bytes versus binary masks; generic PCA matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific result.
boundaries: Synthetic thresholded low-rank mask family only
No trained SupSup/Piggyback models or language task evidence
Teacher family is aligned to a two-dimensional shared score basis
Exact binary masks are the strongest storage/quality control
